newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria at odds with Gazprom on gas pric.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria at odds with Gazprom on gas pric.

text.p: Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said on Friday Bulgaria would insist on receiving Russian natural gas directly from producer RAO Gazprom, not at higher prices through an intermediary.
Kostov, answering questions in parliament, said Gazprom had offered gas for Bulgaria to be supplied through Overgas Inc, a subsidiary of Gazprom and Bulgarian conglomerate Multigroup.

"The government through (state gas distributor) Bulgargas made several offers for direct negotiations with the producer -- Gazprom or Gazexport," Kostov said. "Unfortunately, these offers have not yet met the understanding of the other side."
Kostov said he had been told by his counterparts in other countries "from Estonia to Romania and Georgia" that they received Russian gas directly from Gazprom or its exporting arm Gazexport.

"The most essential part of the offer is a purchase price of $99 per 1,000 cubic metres (of gas) which is higher by $10-15 compared to European prices," Kostov said. European countries were buying gas for $60 to $84 per 1,000 cubic metres, he added.
Kostov said attempts by other firms to supply Russian gas to Bulgaria had failed due to Gazprom's refusal. He did not name the firms.
Bulgaria and Russia signed in April in Moscow an intergovernmental agreement on the transit of Russian gas to the Balkans and construction of new pipelines.
Bulgaria has a 2,200-km pipeline network, including 625 km of transit pipelines which receive and transmit gas from outside the country.
Kostov said Bulgaria had not benefited significantly from existing transiting pipelines but the government was in favour of realising new projects for transiting Russian gas.
The pipeline to Greece, which cost $180 million to build and has an annual capacity of 1.5 billion cubic metres, carries only token quantities of gas.
A pipeline to Macedonia built two years ago is lying idle filled with gas as Bulgaria's western neighbour has not completed construction work on its territory. -- Sofia Newsroom, +359-2-91188
